page: OVHcloud b3-32 is a general-purpose virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32 GB of system memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is provisioned with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and one complimentary public IPv4 address under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also strong at 96.92 GB/sec, complemented by a high PassMark memory score. Multi-core CPU performance, memory read bandwidth, and database operations on Redis and PassMark fall within the average range. Text processing benchmarks show strong results, while software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing perform at average levels. For machine learning, the instance achieves strong text generation speeds on small 135M models, though performance on medium 7B models remains average.

The b3-32 instance offers a balanced resource profile, delivering dedicated AMD EPYC cores and NVMe storage without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. This configuration is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, text processing, software compilation, and moderate database operations.
description: The OVHcloud b3-32 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.3 GHz with no hyperthreading, paired with 32 GB of RAM to maintain a balanced 1:4 resource ratio. Storage is supported by a bundled 200 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a 2 Gbps baseline. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, high memory write bandwidth, and strong text processing capabilities, while multi-core operations and database tasks perform at average levels. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures stable performance, making this instance a cost-effective option for general-purpose applications, web serving, software compilation, and text processing workloads.
